properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 2 at 3:06AM EDT until August 2 at 8:30AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
...FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 830 AM EDT THIS
MORNING FOR NORTHEASTERN SURRY COUNTY...

At 306 AM EDT, severe flash flooding continues as several creeks and
rivers are well out of their banks and continue to rise due to
runoff from very heavy rain earlier this evening. This resulted in
numerous water rescues in the Mt. Airy and Pilot Mountain areas
earlier in the night. The Ararat River continues to rise extremely
quickly, with the river in Mt. Airy above major flood stage,
observed at nearly 29.0 feet shortly before 3 AM. Rutledge Creek,
Seed Cane Creek, Faulkner Creek, and Big Creek may still be rising
as well. Numerous roads are flooded and impassible, including East
Pine Street, Riverside Drive, Westfield Road, and Welcome Baptist
Church Road. This is a very dangerous situation as motorists may
unknowingly drive into deep flood waters, not realizing the flooding
is there due to the darkness.

This is a FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for areas surrounding the towns of
Mt. Airy and Pilot Mountain. This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS
SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! Life threatening flash flooding of low water
crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Airy...                      Flat Rock...
Pilot Mountain...                  Cana...
Woodville...                       Ararat...
Westfield...

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Archies Creek, Bull Creek, Ararat River and Big Creek.
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now! This is an extremely dangerous and
life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are
fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order. If
you must travel, make sure somebody knows were you are going, and
the route you plan to take to your destination. If you encounter a
flooded road, turn around. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles. Be
especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding. Do not drive around barricades.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather
Service by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports
and pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Stokes, NC; Surry, NC; Patrick, VA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 2 at 1:41AM EDT until August 2 at 5:30AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
At 141 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicates heavy rain has exited the
warned area this morning. However, thunderstorms earlier this
evening produced between 4 and locally 7.5 inches of rain in eastern
Surry County, western Stokes County, and southwest Patrick County.
The heaviest rainfall has occurred in the Ararat River basin, which
is approaching a stage of 24 feet as of 130 AM. Both Surry County
and Stokes County Emergency Management staff reported that severe
flooding is occurring, with Big Creek observed well out of its banks
and flowing across both Old Asbury Road and Frans Road in the
Westfield area. Flooding is likely also occurring along Meadow
Branch and Pinch Gut Creek. Numerous swift water rescues have
occurred, and many rivers and creeks continue to rise as runoff
collects in the waterways.


HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.  Many
creeks and rivers are still rising despite heavy rain
having exited the warned area.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Airy...                      Flat Rock...
Pilot Mountain...                  Danbury...
Francisco...                       Ararat...
Cana...
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles. Be especially cautious at night when it is
harder to recognize the dangers of flooding.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather

properties.instruction:

may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.instruction:

may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as
forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Surry, NC; Carroll, VA; Floyd, VA; Patrick, VA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 2 at 2:52AM EDT until August 2 at 4:30AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
At 252 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicates heavy rain has exited the
warned area this morning. However, thunderstorms earlier this
evening produced between 3.5 and locally 6.5 inches of rain across
portions of Carroll, Patrick and Floyd Counties. Runoff from this
rain continues to collect in area creeks and rivers, causing them to
rise rapidly. Many roads remain flooded and impassible due to
flooding, or flooding related debris covering the roads. This is a
dangerous situation as some roads remain flooded this morning, with
the potential that motorists may unknowingly drive into deep flood
waters, not realizing the flooding is there due to the darkness.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Airy...                      Flat Rock...
Hillsville...                      Dobson...
Stuart...                          Floyd...
Willis...

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Big Indian Creek, Beaver Creek, Beaverdam Creek, Anglin Branch,
Archies Creek and Ararat River.
properties.instruction:
Because of the potential for flooded roads, people are advised to
avoid all travel unless absolutely necessary. If you must travel,
make sure somebody knows were you are going, and the route you plan
to take to your destination. If you encounter a flooded road, turn
around. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles. Be especially cautious
at night when it is harder to recognize the dangers of flooding.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather
Service by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports
and pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.
